aaa_enabled.summary: Configure TACACS+ or RADIUS authentication in config_db.
cli: config aaa authentication login tacacs+ local
aaa_enabled.notes: SONiC supports TACACS+ and RADIUS via config_db AAA and TACACS_SERVER/RADIUS_SERVER tables.

secure_vty_transport.summary: Disable telnet; SSH is the only supported remote management protocol.
secure_vty_transport.notes: SONiC does not typically run telnet. Verify with 'show feature status telnet'.

vty_idle_timeout.summary: Configure SSH idle timeout in sshd_config.
vty_idle_timeout.notes: SSH idle timeout is managed at the Linux level (sshd_config ClientAliveInterval/ClientAliveCountMax), not in config_db.json.

enable_secret_encrypted.summary: Manage user credentials at the Linux level.
enable_secret_encrypted.notes: SONiC user credentials are managed via Linux passwd/shadow. Use strong passwords and consider disabling password authentication in favour of SSH keys.

no_default_snmp_community.summary: Remove default SNMP community strings from config_db.

http_server_disabled.summary: Disable the REST API if not needed.
http_server_disabled.notes: The REST API availability depends on the SONiC image build.

ssh_version_2.summary: Verify SSH protocol version in sshd_config.
ssh_version_2.notes: SSH version is configured at the Linux level. Modern SONiC enforces SSHv2 by default.

logging_enabled.notes: SONiC uses rsyslog for local logging, which runs independently of config_db.

management_acl.summary: Apply a control-plane ACL to restrict management access.
cli: config acl add table SSH_ONLY CTRLPLANE --stage ingress --service SSH
config acl add rule SSH_ONLY RULE_1 --SRC_IP <mgmt-subnet>/24 --PACKET_ACTION FORWARD --PRIORITY 100
config acl add rule SSH_ONLY DEFAULT --PACKET_ACTION DROP --PRIORITY 1
management_acl.notes: Control-plane ACLs (type CTRLPLANE) restrict access to management services.

login_banner.summary: Configure the login banner via /etc/motd or sshd_config Banner.
login_banner.notes: Login banners are managed at the Linux level, not in config_db.json.

password_min_length.notes: Password policies are managed via PAM (pam_pwquality) at the Linux level.

ntp_configured.notes: Two sources let the device detect a lying one.
